subject_rule: Limited to the programme's fields: fellows are placed in a cohort at one of 7 host universities 'based on the host university's impact areas and the Fellows' professional expertise', and are 'assigned ... based on their area of interest and professional field'; the site names six fields of study (Communications and Journalism; Law and Governance; Natural Resources Policy; Public and Economic Policy; Public Health Policy and Management; Technology Policy and Management). No degree is awarded and no particular academic degree subject is required beyond an undergraduate degree.

notes: Recorded 21 rows for the diploma (non-degree fellowship) level: 7 host-university fields (one row per university), 6 fields of study from the Fields of Study page, and 8 further fields that appear only on the Eligibility page (that page lists 12 field entries; those repeating fields already above are not duplicated).

The site gives two overlapping field lists: the Fields of Study page (6 fields) and the Eligibility page (12 entries in four impact areas). The Eligibility list may be older and not current. The host page's competition schedule 2025 to 2029 also names fields such as Substance Abuse Education and Policy, Economic Policy and Finance, Agricultural and Rural Development and Educational Administration, Planning and Policy without naming universities.
Host universities change over time (five-year cycles chosen by competition); the 7 hosts listed are the current ones on the host page.
Applicants need an undergraduate degree (any subject stated) and 5 years of professional experience; the professional field must match a host impact area.
